name: Paxillus involutus
notes: Long-distance exploration type [13]; a gilled relative of the boletes. Reported (unchecked) to be the model for how mycorrhizal fungi break down organic matter, to be easy in culture and to have a sequenced genome.

tip_speed.source: Kim C.-G., Power S.A., Bell J.N.B. 2004, Effects of cadmium on radial growth and dry mass production of ectomycorrhizal fungi, Korean Journal of Ecology 27(5):301-306
tip_speed.note: control (no cadmium) colonies of isolate 87017 on MMN agar at 20 C in the dark: 5.23 +/- 0.10 mm/day, n = 6, from a regression of colony diameter on time (Table 1). Halved to a radius rate of 2.62 mm/day, x 41.7 = 109 um/h. Measured at 20 C; the optimum temperature is not known, so no correction is made. The paper notes that other studies found this species slower than Suillus bovinus, so isolates differ

uptake_rate.note: tuning value, set to tip speed / segment length so that one feeding segment can supply about one growing tip; no measurement found

transport_speed.source: Timonen S., Finlay R.D., Olsson S., Soderstrom B. 1996, Dynamics of phosphorus translocation in intact ectomycorrhizal systems: non-destructive monitoring using a beta-scanner, FEMS Microbiology Ecology 19(3):171-180
transport_speed.note: minimum velocity of 32P-phosphate through intact mycelium to Pinus contorta roots, 7.5 mm/h, from the abstract; a lower bound worked out by the authors from a 15 cm path and the 20 to 50 h lag. Reported for Paxillus involutus and Suillus variegatus together, not separately. The true speed may be higher
